title: Tool‑Augmented Post‑Processing of Identical LLM Candidates for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration (shared_initial_candidate evaluation)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (cand_netops_toolagent_003_v1) to isolate whether deterministic post‑processing (a topology‑aware deterministic validator + lightweight simulator) changes a binary validator pass/fail verdict when both pipelines receive the identical single LLM candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Design: 300 paired tasks, single shared LLM generation per task reused verbatim by both pipelines; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Completed: 598 episodes → 299 analyzable pairs. Result (artifact‑grounded): contingency n11=299, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0 → paired diff = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00] (10k resamples, seed=1729). No repair calls were invoked in the completed episodes (model_calls_used = 300; no repair_applied true flags observed). One preregistered pair excluded after a provider failure; all raw artifacts, provider traces, scoring JSONs (validator_trace included), analysis inputs/outputs, and the preregistration are archived and SHA‑256 hashed for audit. We discuss the ceiling effect that renders the preregistered minimally important effect untestable here, clarify pipeline semantics and repair accounting using archived evidence, and provide artifact‑grounded guidance for follow‑ups.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are being proposed to automate NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, configuration repair, and playbook enactment. Typical agentic architectures couple an LLM generator with deterministic post‑processing (validators, simulators or checkers) to raise operational trustworthiness. When evaluating such systems, reported gains may mix generator improvements and verifier/simulator effects. To isolate the latter we preregistered a narrowly scoped confirmatory experiment: when the identical single LLM candidate is supplied verbatim to both a baseline and a guarded pipeline (shared_initial_candidate semantics), does deterministic post‑processing change the binary deterministic‑validator pass/fail outcome? This run strictly followed preregistration cand_netops_toolagent_003_v1 (SHA‑256: 991674d51794b41cf66471509149237b9a99f709b69aa3408d3d9d2ea2d50fc0) and archives all artifacts and hashes for independent verification.
sections.related_work: Prior work motivates tool‑augmented agent architectures and intent→configuration tasks (representative verified items used for positioning include Nguyen et al., 2024; PreConfig (arXiv:2403.09369); and a practical tool‑augmented AIOps case study (Rong Lu, preprint 2026)). These works argue for validators and simulators in operational pipelines. Our contribution is methodological and empirical: an artifact‑archived, preregistered isolation of the validator/simulator effect under shared candidate semantics, complementing previous studies that compare independent generation strategies.
sections.methodology: Preregistration (frozen plan). The preregistration cand_netops_toolagent_003_v1 fixed: (1) research question and primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on a deterministic‑validator pass indicator; (2) shared_initial_candidate semantics (one LLM call per task reused verbatim by both pipelines); (3) paired design with 300 tasks (150 simple, 150 complex); (4) analysis executor = paired_binary_analysis_v1 (exact McNemar two‑sided + paired bootstrap percentile CI, 10k resamples, seed=1729); (5) complete‑pair handling and exclusion rules (e.g., provider failures → exclude pair and log). The preregistration JSON (SHA‑256 above) is archived. Execution contract & resources. Declared generator: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic validator implementation: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (scorer_version 5.0) invoked identically by both pipelines as the post‑processing component (scoring JSONs include validator_trace with final_state and difficulty metadata). Shared candidate semantics and reuse. For each task the system produced one LLM generation (the shared_initial candidate), stored it, and fed that exact candidate, without modification, to both the baseline and guarded scoring paths. Example artifacts proving reuse: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256: 8f38c8becd7e...) and the matched scoring outputs execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256: 6569b491dbf...) and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256: cefa6344888a...). Repair policy and model‑call budget. The preregistered maximum model calls = 600 (one generation + at most one repair call per task). Observed model_calls_used = 300 (one generation per task; see execution manifest field model_calls_used = 300), indicating no extra model calls for repair during completed episodes. Validator behavior. The deterministic validator enforces domain invariants (make‑before‑break, shutdown→change→restore, minimum active constraints), parses command fragments to a normalized_configuration, produces a boolean pass/fail, enumerates violation codes, and emits a final_state snapshot. All scoring JSONs include the validator_trace block for audit. Task corpus and simulator. Tasks were deterministically sampled from a synthetic topology pool; each manifest line includes the natural‑language intent, initial_state, expected_final_state, difficulty tags, and required_sequence (see execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Stopping, failures, and missingness. The run stopped when all shared generations were attempted. One shared generation failed (pair‑000269) due to a provider error and was excluded per the preregistered complete‑pair rule; failure traces and logs are archived (execution/provider_calls/task-000269-shared-initial.json). Analysis. The paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor produced contingency counts, exact McNemar p, and bootstrap CI (10k resamples, seed=1729). All analysis artifacts are archived (analysis/*; paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256: d77df43abf83e...).

Baseline success rate = 299/299 = 100.0%; guarded success rate = 299/299 = 100.0%. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00,0.00] (10k resamples, seed=1729; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256: 7364d6a1...). Repair and repair‑call accounting (required revision resolved). Consistently, the validator_trace / scoring JSONs show repair_applied=false for representative episodes (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256: 6569b491dbf... and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256: cefa6344888a...). Secondary estimands. Because there are no discordant pairs, secondary exploratory estimands (simulated outage difference, subgroup deltas) are uninformative for confirmatory testing; raw traces remain archived for exploratory inspection.
sections.discussion: Primary scientific interpretation. Under the shared_initial_candidate semantics and the synthetic task distribution used here, deterministic post‑processing (the validator + simulator) confirmed rather than changed the binary acceptance decision: every analyzable shared candidate that the baseline path accepted was also accepted by the guarded path (n11 = 299; no discordant outcomes). This artifact‑grounded outcome is exact in our archived inputs and outputs (see analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256: d77df43abf83e...). Statistical implications and the degenerate contingency. The observed contingency is degenerate (all pairs fall in the n11 cell). Consequences: (1) exact McNemar returns p = 1.0 because there are zero discordant pairs; (2) paired bootstrap under the percentile method (10k resamples, seed=1729) yields an empirically degenerate CI [0.00,0.00] because all resampled paired differences are zero. These behaviors are expected and documented in the archived analysis log (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256: 7364d6a1...). Importantly, the preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline success ≈ 0.60 and a minimally important paired improvement of 0.20; the observed baseline = 1.00 creates a ceiling effect that makes the preregistered target effect untestable in this run. Operational and methodological implications. (A) When generator candidates meeting validator invariants are present, the validator's operational value is primarily auditable justification and explicit violation encoding (validator_trace), rather than changing binary acceptance. (B) To measure end‑to‑end benefits of tool‑augmented agents researchers must allow generator behaviors to differ across conditions (no shared reuse), include adversarial/harder task strata to avoid ceiling effects, and replicate across model families and seeds. Artifact‑grounded recommendations for follow‑ups. Use the archived scoring and provider traces format (execution/scoring/*.json and execution/provider_calls/*.json) to implement: (1) independent per‑condition generation experiments; (2) adversarial task injection that raises baseline failure probability; (3) ablations of repair‑loop counts (iter=1 vs iter≥2) while logging repair_applied and repair_provider_trace files; (4) multi‑model replications. Limitations (artifact‑grounded). (1) Shared_initial semantics isolate post‑processing only and therefore cannot assess whether tool‑augmented generation would produce improved candidates. (2) Synthetic topology pool and lightweight simulator — external validity to vendor‑specific CLIs and production devices is limited. (3) Single declared model family (gpt‑5‑mini) — cross‑model generality requires replication. (4) The deterministic validator encodes curated invariants and is not exhaustive of all production device behavior. All limitations and recommended follow‑ups are artifact‑traceable in the archive.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a focused confirmatory experiment to answer whether deterministic post‑processing changes a validator pass/fail verdict when identical LLM candidates are reused by both pipelines. For 299 analyzable pairs we observed n11=299 and no discordant pairs; paired difference = 0.00 (exact McNemar p = 1.0; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00], 10k resamples, seed=1729). Model_calls_used = 300; no repair calls were invoked (aggregated repair_applied true count = 0). The evidence is fully archived and SHA‑256 hashed for independent audit. The main scientific implication is narrow: in a regime with high‑quality generator outputs that already satisfy the validator invariants, deterministic post‑processing provides machine‑readable auditability and diagnostics but does not alter the binary accept decision. Broader claims about tool‑augmented agent benefits require experiments that (i) do not reuse shared candidates, (ii) include adversarial/harder tasks to avoid ceiling effects, and (iii) replicate across models and device repertoires. The full reproducibility bundle (responses, provider traces, scoring JSONs with validator_trace, analysis artifacts, and preregistration) is archived for independent verification; representative file paths and SHA‑256s are given in the Disclosure Statement below.

All analysis inputs and outputs are archived (analysis/*) and hashed.
- Reproducibility bundle, provenance and hashes: all raw responses, provider traces, scoring JSONs with validator_trace, task manifests, execution logs, and a full per‑file SHA‑256 manifest are archived under execution/ and analysis/. Representative paths and SHA‑256s cited above enable independent verification. The full per‑file mapping is available in the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) and the included artifact map (see execution manifest). - Human involvement and autonomy boundary: pre‑lock human activity included selection of the NetOps topic family and development/testing of the autonomous pipeline. After the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature discovery, preregistration, experiment design, code generation, execution, analysis, peer review, and manuscript generation. No human manual editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock. Deviations, restarts, and failures (the single provider failure) are logged and archived. The master prompt archive (path above and SHA‑256) documents the autonomy boundary as required.
- Limitations (concise, artifact‑referenced): (1) shared_initial semantics isolate only post‑processing and cannot measure whether tool‑augmented generation improves candidate quality; (2) synthetic task pool and lightweight simulator limit external validity to vendor CLIs and production devices; (3) single declared model family (gpt‑5‑mini) — replication required for cross‑model claims; (4) deterministic validator encodes curated invariants and is not exhaustive; (5) observed baseline = 1.00 created a ceiling effect that prevented testing of the preregistered minimally important effect. All limitations and the files supporting them (scoring JSONs, task manifests, execution manifest, and analysis logs) are archived and SHA‑256 hashed.
limitations: Shared_initial semantics isolate only post‑processing and therefore cannot assess whether tool‑augmented generation (allowing generator repairs or verifier‑guided generation) would improve candidate quality.
Task set is synthetic and executed in a lightweight simulator; external validity to vendor‑specific CLIs, firmware idiosyncrasies, and production telemetry is limited.
Only one declared model family (gpt‑5‑mini) was used; results do not generalize across models without replication.

Deterministic validator encodes curated workflow invariants (make‑before‑break, shutdown_configure_restore, minimum‑active rules) but cannot exhaustively represent all production device behaviors or operator policies.
Observed baseline success = 100% produced a ceiling effect, rendering the preregistered minimally important effect (0.20) untestable in this run.
